title: Troubleshoot M365 with AI: from symptom to verdict
summary: A missing receipt label makes a small case you can prove from start to finish.

intro.what: AI can help you choose what to check next. You own the evidence and the decision. A clear answer with no row to support it is still a guess.
intro.features: Use a case note with six boxes: symptom, possible cause, evidence needed, one test, expected result and verdict. Record what happened before and after a fix.
intro.exchange: Trace one receipt from a report to a new delivery test.
intro.m365: Keep a sign-in guess separate from the policy result that could prove it.
intro.developer: Reproduce a broken label, then try a second input that should stay unchanged.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read a cloud message trace
Microsoft Learn · inspect a mail flow rule
Microsoft Learn · supported rule changes and WhatIf

sections.title: Give the helper a small, useful case
paragraphs: Write the exact symptom first: “Training receipts arrive without the expected label.” Add the UTC window, which messages are affected, the error text if there is one, and one message that works. Keep the original in its approved store. Share only approved, stripped-down fields.

Open Lab 13 or the practice kit and read change-card.txt. Hide C3 through C7 for your first pass. Ask the helper for two causes, one piece of evidence that would decide each, and one read-only test. Ask it to say “unknown” when the data stops.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read a cloud message trace
Microsoft Learn · inspect a mail flow rule

sections.title: Make each guess earn a test
paragraphs: A missing label could mean the receipt never arrived or the rule missed its subject. If the first idea is right, the receiving test should lack the message. If the second is right, the receipt arrives plain and its subject differs from the stored rule word.
Read C1 and C3. Delivery happened in this case. The rule looks for “invioce” and the receipt says “invoice.” Mark the second idea supported. Keep other messages and other rules outside your verdict.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read a cloud message trace
Microsoft Learn · inspect a mail flow rule

sections.title: Separate a proposed change from a verified fix
paragraphs: Read C4 for the one approved practice edit. Before any real change, record the current value, who approves, a stop condition and how to restore that value. Check the exact cmdlet, environment and parameters on Microsoft Learn. Inspect the current state first. Use WhatIf only when the command supports it. A preview cannot prove how a new message travels.

Read W3 and W4 in review-window.csv. The fresh receipt is tagged and the ordinary message is plain. You can call the fix verified for these probes. If only W3 were present, the effect on ordinary mail would be unknown. Give the next operator the evidence IDs and the rollback note.
sources: Microsoft Learn · inspect a mail flow rule
Microsoft Learn · supported rule changes and WhatIf

title: One message, two delivery results
summary: A message trace shows where to look next. A matching bounce can explain why a particular copy failed.

intro.what: A message trace follows mail through Exchange. A non-delivery report, or NDR, tells the sender about a failed delivery. Let the AI match the two records before it explains the failure.
intro.features: Give the helper a small time window, a message ID and made-up recipient labels. Ask for a separate claim and row for each recipient. Add the bounce only after it tells you which fact is missing.
intro.exchange: Tell a service desk which copy of a message failed and which copy reached its recipient.
intro.m365: Show a support team which facts belong in its incident note and which ones still need checking.
intro.developer: Use the same method when a reminder app sends one alert to several people.
sources: Microsoft Learn · follow a message through Exchange Online

sections.title: Make the subject line a bad shortcut
paragraphs: Open trace-recipients.csv in the practice kit. All four subjects say Dock sheet. Ask about parcel-41 only. Put a finger beside each row with that exact message ID. There are two. T3 has the same sender and subject but belongs to another send.

Read the two recipient addresses and statuses back to the helper. Dock shows Delivered and stores shows Failed. Neither row shows whether a person opened the message. The summary alone gives no reason for the failure.
sources: Microsoft Learn · follow a message through Exchange Online
Microsoft Learn · Get-MessageTraceV2 in Exchange Online

sections.title: Give each guess a test
paragraphs: Write two possible causes before opening the next file. A missing recipient should leave an address lookup error. A mail rule that blocked delivery would need evidence of that rule’s action. Ask which single record could separate them.

Open ndr-recipient.txt. Match N1 to the message ID and N2 to the failed address. N4 and N5 give a lookup error. Ask whether the bounce alone tells you who entered the address or whether a mailbox was deleted. Both answers are still unknown.
sources: Microsoft Learn · follow a message through Exchange Online

sections.title: Record a fix you can check
paragraphs: Open alias-check.txt. A3 names the active Supply address. A4 shows the old entry in one list. A5 records approval for a correction in that list only. Read the results of two fresh sends in A6 and A7.

A ticket can now say which entry changed and which test passed. It can also say “Other senders and lists were outside this test.” If someone claims every lost message is fixed, ask for the fresh send that supports that claim.
sources: Microsoft Learn · follow a message through Exchange Online

exercise.prompt: A teammate says T4 proves the original parcel reached the Supply desk. What two cells would you compare?
answer: Compare the message ID and the recipient. T4 concerns parcel-43 and supply, whereas T2 concerns parcel-41 and stores. T4 helps form a guess. N1, N2 and A4 let you test it.

title: Read a mail header before changing DNS
summary: Test an AI’s SPF, DKIM and DMARC explanation against a stamped result and a dated DNS snapshot.

intro.what: A receiver leaves a short record of its checks in the message header. Ask the AI to read the result for this one message, then test each possible cause against the records from that time.
intro.features: SPF checks a sending source. DKIM checks a signature. DMARC asks whether at least one passing check lines up with the visible From domain. Each check tells you something different.
intro.exchange: Separate a failing bulletin from another message that used the same From address.
intro.m365: Give a security reviewer the smallest set of fields needed to check an authentication claim.
intro.developer: When an app sends notices, compare the records from a failing send and a known working send.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read the authentication results in mail headers
Microsoft Learn · check which senders an SPF record lists
Microsoft Learn · DKIM signing domains and selectors
Microsoft Learn · DMARC domain alignment and policy

sections.title: Read the receiver’s own copy
paragraphs: Open auth-header.txt. H2 gives the message ID. H6 names sink.example.test, the receiver that supplied this saved header. On H6, find the SPF result beside smtp.mailfrom, the DKIM result beside header.d and the DMARC result beside header.from.

Write down each result before guessing a cause. H1 gives the incoming IP. H5 gives the signing domain and selector, a label for the key the receiver looks up. H7 leaves the final mailbox outcome open.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read the authentication results in mail headers
Microsoft Learn · DKIM signing domains and selectors

sections.title: Test the source and the signing key
paragraphs: Open auth-dns.txt. Read the last number of the incoming IP in H1 and the authorized IP in D1. The sample sender ends in 44. The record lists 24. Ask the helper to cite both lines before it blames SPF.

Join the selector in H5 to the signing domain. D2 is the lookup for that exact name. It found no such name a minute after receipt. That supports a missing-key explanation for DKIM. An exact replay of what the receiver saw at 10:04 would need its lookup record from then. D4 also leaves the approved owner of the sending IP unknown.
sources: Microsoft Learn · check which senders an SPF record lists
Microsoft Learn · DKIM signing domains and selectors
Microsoft Learn · read the authentication results in mail headers

sections.title: Make the helper explain the other message
paragraphs: D3 shows strict alignment for both checks. In D5 the envelope and visible domains match exactly. SPF passed. That single aligned pass is enough for DMARC even though DKIM failed. Ask the helper to explain why this case can differ from H6.

Ask it to predict final delivery from D3 alone. A published quarantine policy is not a receipt. Confirm delivery or quarantine with a separate receiving-side record for the message. Leave that outcome unknown for beacon-17.
sources: Microsoft Learn · DMARC domain alignment and policy
Microsoft Learn · read the authentication results in mail headers

exercise.prompt: What can the team tell the sending service right now?
answer: Report the IP mismatch and the missing selector name with their times. Request the approved sender list and the receiver’s original DNS evidence before proposing a repair.

title: Why an enabled mail rule never tags the notice
summary: Trace a missing subject label from the intended rule through a narrow fix and two controls.

intro.what: A transport rule has a test and an action. In this case, a delivered message reaches the right mailbox, but the subject never gets the label the team needs.
intro.features: Ask the AI for one row per condition. Give each row the required value, the observed value and a yes or no. Check the actual incoming subject before reading the result.
intro.exchange: Explain a mail flow rule that never matches the intended board notices.
intro.m365: Write an approval note that limits a correction to one field on one rule.
intro.developer: Test a notification filter with an expected match and two examples that should stay unchanged.
sources: Microsoft Learn · mail flow rule conditions
Microsoft Learn · mail flow rule actions
Microsoft Learn · test a mail flow rule

sections.title: Find the first false condition
paragraphs: Open rule-snapshot.txt and find B1 in rule-retest.csv. Read SentTo and SubjectContainsWords as separate tests. B1 meets the recipient test. Its subject contains PIER. R5 requires the word PIERX.

The rule is enabled and set to Enforce in this copy. R6 describes a subject label. The missing label is the symptom. Delivery itself worked. If the AI recommends changing routing, ask it to point to a failed delivery in B1.
sources: Microsoft Learn · mail flow rule conditions
Microsoft Learn · mail flow rule actions
Microsoft Learn · read a transport rule

sections.title: Predict the boundary
paragraphs: R7 is the approved requirement. Write a small test grid before you read any After rows. A PIER notice to board should get the label. A FERRY notice to board should stay plain. A PIER notice to office should also stay plain.

Changing the subject test alone fits the request. Keep the recipient and action fixed. Before reading R8, write a rollback note: restore PIERX on Board ticket label if a control gets a label or the target stops delivering. Keep the old record and ask the owner to review the test result.
sources: Microsoft Learn · mail flow rule conditions
Microsoft Learn · test a mail flow rule

sections.title: Decide whether to close the case
paragraphs: In rule-retest.csv compare B1 with V1. Both were delivered, but only V1 has the label in its received subject. The two new control sends V2 and V3 stayed plain. Use their own message IDs in your note.

The change in R8 and these three results support closing the ticket for this rule and these cases. A fresh date or different route needs its own evidence. In an actual change window the team owns approval, timing, tests and rollback. This exercise reads recorded practice results.
sources: Microsoft Learn · test a mail flow rule
Microsoft Learn · follow a message through Exchange Online

exercise.prompt: If V2 also had [BOARD], could you call the repair verified?
answer: No. A subject outside the requested word would have received the label. Keep the ticket open and follow the agreed rollback plan.

title: Which sign-in did the device policy block?
summary: A tablet cannot open mail. Put the sign-in and the device report side by side before blaming an access policy.

intro.what: Ask AI to explain one sign-in. Give it the event, resource, device label and time. Ask which row supports each claim.
intro.features: An Entra event can show results for several access policies. Intune can show a device’s compliance state. AI can line up these records. You decide if they describe the same attempt.
intro.exchange: Separate an app sign-in block from a mail delivery failure.
intro.m365: Compare one blocked sign-in with one successful sign-in to the same resource.
intro.developer: Put an event label on each app error so two failures close in time can be told apart.
sources: Microsoft Learn · review the Conditional Access result for a sign-in
Microsoft Learn · read Intune device compliance reports

sections.title: Find the failed attempt
paragraphs: Open entra-signins.csv in the practice kit. The report in identity-case-notes.txt names EV-31. In the CSV, look for that event, the Mail resource and tab-7 at 09:04 UTC. Two rows match one sign-in. Count the event once.

Ask the helper for the policy name, the mode and the result on each row. Microsoft explains that a policy in report-only mode records a result. It does not enforce its grant controls. In this case, the policy called Managed tablet was on and its device check failed. Preview gate also shows failure, but ran in report-only mode.
sources: Microsoft Learn · review the Conditional Access result for a sign-in

sections.title: Join on the device and the time
paragraphs: Cover the lines after 09:04 UTC. Give the helper the sign-in rows and the earlier Intune rows. Ask it which device fact was available when the block happened. I1 is the earlier state for tab-7. I2 belongs to another tablet. I3 comes later.

Ask what remains unknown. The old OS and the failed grant fit together in this case. A snapshot on its own cannot prove what happened at sign-in. If the device label or time is missing, ask for that evidence and leave the cause open.
sources: Microsoft Learn · review the Conditional Access result for a sign-in
Microsoft Learn · read Intune device compliance reports

rows: One enforced failure and one report-only result.
The tablet was below the required OS.
Mail worked on tab-4, even with the report-only failure.

sections.title: Close the loop with a fresh sign-in
paragraphs: Predict what you expect after the approved device update. Tab-7 should report the required OS, its enabled grant should pass and the same Mail resource should open. Now reveal N2, I3, S5 and N3. They meet all three checks. Record the result for tab-7 only.
If the device reported compliant but the next sign-in still failed, ask for the new event and its applied policies. An AI summary of the old attempt cannot stand in for a new test.
sources: Microsoft Learn · review the Conditional Access result for a sign-in
Microsoft Learn · read Intune device compliance reports

title: Trace one hybrid handoff
summary: A cloud message stalls on its way to an on-premises mailbox. Mark the direction, expected host and actual host before proposing a repair.

intro.what: A message takes a route. Give AI the sender side, recipient side and one test marker. Ask it to join just the records for that route.
intro.features: A cloud outbound connector and an on-premises receive connector have different jobs. A connector setting tells you the intended setup. A receipt can show where a particular test message arrived.
intro.exchange: Match an Exchange Online sending route to the intended on-premises destination.
intro.m365: Use a separate test for each direction when two services exchange a file.
intro.developer: Compare the address an app used with the address its test plan approved.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read an Exchange Online outbound connector
Microsoft Learn · read an on-premises receive connector

sections.title: Draw one arrow
paragraphs: Open hybrid-route.txt from the practice kit and read lines H1 through H5. Write the direction as cloud to on-premises. H1 names the approved target. H2 records the cloud setting. H4 names the host actually tried. H3 says the intended receiving service was ready. H3 has no arrival for TEST-41.

Have the helper give two possible causes and one test that separates them. A wrong destination and a problem at the intended listener make different predictions about which host the failed attempt used. The name in H4 agrees with H2 and differs from H1. A timeout alone would leave both explanations open.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read an Exchange Online outbound connector
Microsoft Learn · read an on-premises receive connector

sections.title: Use the right read-only command
paragraphs: For the sending side, use the Exchange Online session and the Microsoft Learn page for Get-OutboundConnector. For the receiving side, use the on-premises Exchange session and the page for Get-ReceiveConnector. Each command has an Identity parameter. Check that the returned name is exactly the connector requested. An empty or wrong identity can return a broader list.

Before using a proposed command, find its exact parameters in the official syntax and check the command available in the connected session. Lab 12 supplies separate read-only examples and writes each result to its own new CSV. The offline case can be solved entirely from the text file.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read an Exchange Online outbound connector
Microsoft Learn · read an on-premises receive connector
Microsoft Learn · export a CSV file

sections.title: Test the same direction after the recorded change
paragraphs: H5 is a good test in the reverse direction. It cannot close the original incident. Before reading H6 through H8, predict the host and the destination receipt a successful cloud-to-site test must show.

H6 records an owner’s change. H7 has a fresh marker on the right host and in the destination mailbox. H8 covers a separate unchanged route. In your verdict, record the target and the time of each test. Keep open any question that neither test answers.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read an Exchange Online outbound connector

title: Give four tools the same mail case
summary: Which helper notices a useful control, spots a missing setting and asks for one safe test? Score the first replies yourself.

intro.what: A fair trial gives each helper the same case. Here one mailbox refuses a large message. The same sender can reach another mailbox with the same message.
intro.features: You can run the case online or learn to score a sample reply offline. The kit keeps the first prompt, the key and the later test results apart.
intro.exchange: See which reply uses the small-message and second-recipient controls to narrow a mail fault.
intro.m365: Try the same method with a sign-in that fails on only one device. Keep a successful sign-in as a control.
intro.developer: Give four helpers the same failed test and one passing test. Check whether they ask for useful evidence before changing code.
sources: Microsoft Learn · read delivery trace results
Microsoft Learn · Exchange Online message size limits

sections.title: Keep every first attempt fair
paragraphs: Open cases/vendor-trial.txt in the practice kit. The same prompt is also printed in troubleshooting lab 16. Copy only the block between BEGIN and END. The scoring key and the later rows stay with you.

Start a fresh approved chat in each of the four products. Paste the same block once. Keep the first answer, even if it is wrong. Skip tools you cannot access. Dates, modes and the names shown on screen help you repeat a run. If you cannot see the model name, record “not shown.”
For example, the catalog entry {{model.claude.sonnet.name}} is a model label. Seeing a name in a catalog does not tell you which model answered. Record only the label shown for that run.
sources: OpenAI Help · start a ChatGPT chat
Google Help · use the Gemini app

sections.title: Score evidence before style
paragraphs: Give one point for each row below. Read the reply beside the original packet. A correct guess without the named evidence misses that point. A type of fault may be likely long before its exact setting is known.

rows: R1 is the failed 14 MB message to Workroom.
R2 shows a small message reached the same recipient.
R3 shows the same sender sent the same large message to Stores. That weakens a sender-wide limit as the cause.
R4 points to a size limit. R5 is a plan. Neither gives the active setting.
Read Workroom’s current receive limit. A limit below 14 MB supports the mailbox theory. If it allows 14 MB, check for another limit on that route.

sources: Microsoft Learn · read delivery trace results
Microsoft Learn · Exchange Online message size limits

sections.title: Practice with a reply you can inspect offline
paragraphs: This reply was written for practice. It is not the output of a named product.

R1 is the failed 14 MB message to Workroom. R2 shows small mail gets there, and R3 shows the same sender can send the large message elsewhere. The active setting is unknown. R4 hints at size, and the plan in R5 may be stale. Change the setting to 20 MB.

It earns four points. It uses R1, R2 and R3 well and keeps the active value unknown. It misses the last point by proposing a change. The missing step is to read the current mailbox limit and say what each possible result would mean.
sources: Microsoft Learn · Exchange Online message size limits

sections.title: Keep an honest run sheet
paragraphs: For each run, note one thing the reply did well and one miss or open question. Do this even when two tools tie. If a tool was unavailable, leave its score blank. The edition did not obtain first replies from these four chat products. Its practice answer has no vendor score.

The four product rows start blank. Record the mode, date and one case fact from each reply. Scores and notes you enter stay in this browser. Keep the full reply and personal details out of these boxes.
sources: OpenAI Help · start a ChatGPT chat
Google Help · use the Gemini app

sections.title: Unseal the later evidence
paragraphs: After scoring all first replies, read V1 through V4. The active value was 10 MB. The approved practice change affected only Workroom. The old 14 MB failure now passes. A 24 MB message is still refused.
Write a one-line verdict with the two retest row IDs. Keep your original first-try scores. A later fact can change your diagnosis without changing what the first replies knew.
sources: Microsoft Learn · Exchange Online message size limits
